label: Financial Scams
description: Alleged and proven financial frauds in India

items.label: Coal Block Allocation Scam
items.context: The CAG estimated the government forfeited ₹1.86 lakh crore by allocating coal blocks through discretionary allotment instead of auctions.

items.label: 2G Spectrum Scam
items.context: The CAG estimated the treasury lost ₹1.76 lakh crore due to spectrum being sold at 2001 prices instead of through competitive auctions.

items.label: Commonwealth Games Scam
items.context: Multiple agencies identified massive over-invoicing and kickbacks in the ₹70,000 crore CWG 2010 preparations in Delhi.

items.label: IL&FS Group Default
items.context: Infrastructure conglomerate IL&FS collapsed with ₹91,000 crore in debt, triggering a liquidity crisis in India's NBFC sector.

items.label: ABG Shipyard Bank Fraud
items.context: India's largest bank fraud case. ABG Shipyard allegedly defrauded 28 banks of ₹22,842 crore through falsified accounts.

items.label: PNB–Nirav Modi Fraud
items.context: Diamantaire Nirav Modi and associates allegedly siphoned ₹13,500 crore from Punjab National Bank using fraudulent Letters of Undertaking.

items.label: Satyam Accounting Scandal
items.context: Ramalinga Raju confessed to inflating Satyam Computer's balance sheet by ₹7,136 crore — India's version of Enron.

items.label: Vijay Mallya Bank Defaults
items.context: Kingfisher Airlines chairman Vijay Mallya fled India with alleged unpaid loans of ₹9,000 crore owed to a consortium of 17 banks.

items.label: Harshad Mehta Securities Scam
items.context: Stockbroker Harshad Mehta manipulated BSE stocks using fraudulently obtained bank funds worth ₹4,025 crore — roughly ₹50,000 crore in today's value.
